title: Quota enforcer cache consistency: fix, incremental rollout, and monitoring playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: After a capacity event during token-rotation maintenance on 2026-03-09, several customer-facing services experienced intermittent 429 spikes. Investigation shows the quota enforcer cache occasionally served stale policy state during concurrent token refresh workflows, causing premature enforcement for valid requests. This ticket tracks the fix, rollout strategy, monitoring, and post-deploy follow-ups.
impact_summary: ~6% of requests to the public text-generation endpoint were incorrectly rate-limited over a 45-minute window, increasing client error rates and SLA breaches for several high-usage customers. Support tickets and automated alerts escalated to on-call.
timeline: 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC: Scheduled token rotation job started in primary region.
2026-03-09 03:18 UTC: Spike of 429s observed; automated mitigation (circuit breaker) triggered for 7 minutes.
2026-03-09 03:25 UTC: Ops routed traffic to secondary region; error rate decreased but intermittent 429s continued.
2026-03-09 04:05 UTC: Preliminary investigation identified cache invalidation gaps in quota-enforcer during concurrent auth refresh calls.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Root cause reproduced in staging with load test harness.
2026-03-11 14:30 UTC: Emergency patch proposed and code review opened (PR #redwood/gateway/2348).
root_cause: The quota enforcer uses an in-memory cache keyed by (customer_id, token_hash). During token rotation, auth service returned updated tokens while old token_hash entries were momentarily present. A race condition in the cache loader allowed a stale enforcement policy to be returned for up to one minute in rare concurrent access patterns. This was exacerbated by previously-merged optimization that bypassed cache validation for signed tokens (PR merged in runtime-1.18).
immediate_mitigation: Rollback the optimization that bypassed cache validation for signed tokens (rollback PR #redwood/gateway/2370).
Increase cache TTL to 120s and enable synchronous invalidation hook from auth service while we ship a proper fix.
Temporarily widen 429 -> 5xx fallback for affected customer routes to avoid client-side throttling cascades.
long_term_mitigations: Refactor quota enforcer cache to persist conservative policy version vectors and atomically swap on invalidation.
Add an event-driven invalidation API between auth and gateway for token rotation events (idempotent, signed), with retries and ack recording.
Introduce canary rollouts with staged TTL/validation increases and synthetic traffic checks before global deploys.
Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent token rotation + high QPS paths (load harness).'
action_items: ENG-17522: Implement atomic cache swap and add policy versioning in quota enforcer (owner: Ravi, estimate: 5).
ENG-17523: Add event-driven invalidation hook and contract between auth and gateway (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate: 3).
ENG-17524: Backfill integration tests into gateway CI for token-rotation race scenarios (owner: Lena Park, estimate: 3).
ENG-17525: Create deployment playbook for staged TTL and validation changes; include rollback steps and KPIs (owner: On-call lead, estimate: 2).
ENG-17526: Dashboard: real-time policy mismatch monitor and 429 anomaly alerting for top 50 customers (owner: Observability team, estimate: 3).
Support: Draft customer communication for affected tenants with timeline and remediation steps (owner: Claire O'Neill, due: 2026-03-13).
acceptance_criteria: No 429 spikes attributable to stale cache in post-deploy 72-hour burn window under synthetic high-concurrency token rotation tests.
Event-driven invalidation receives and ack's rotation events reliably in staging for 1000 concurrent rotations.
New dashboard shows policy mismatch rate below 0.01% for 7 days after rollout.
PRs reviewed and approved by at least one runtime maintainer and one security reviewer.
notes: On-call reported the first anomaly via PagerDuty runbook; initial auto-mitigation reduced customer impact but masked the scope of stale-cache errors.
The signed-token optimization improved median latency by ~4ms but introduced a correctness window under token churn; trade-offs discussed in architecture review.
Security reviewed the proposed event invalidation API; concern around replay protection was addressed with signed nonces.
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Santos): prefer phased rollouts and customer-facing comms prior to full change.
Design (Lena Park): monitor UX regressions for rate-limit messaging in client SDKs and consider client-side retries backoff guidance.
SRE (Eun-Ji Kim): require playbook run-through with on-call before prod deploy; include automated safety gate in CI.
